metadata.description: Multi-producer multi-consumer channels for message passing

classification.reasoning: Purpose: `crossbeam-channel` is a well-known, foundational, and highly popular Rust library for multi-producer multi-consumer message passing (millions of downloads, over 3000 days of age). Sources: none. Sinks: none. Flow: no data flows. Anomalies: none. Unsafe blocks (41 across 4.2k lines, 5.27 per kloc) are entirely expected for a concurrent channel implementation requiring low-level atomics and memory synchronization. The retrieved context documents unrelated past incidents (Telegram C2 in `xrvrv`, proc-macro injection patterns, and `rustdecimal` typosquatting) which bear zero relevance to this legitimate crate. All signals indicate normal, highly trusted crate behavior.

retrieved_context.title: xrvrv Telegram C2 (2023)
retrieved_context.text: Found via manual review of unusual outbound network calls across the crates.io registry's dynamic-analysis dataset. The crate 'xrvrv' established a Telegram bot API connection as a command-and-control channel. This was essentially the only clear confirmed hit from an exhaustive manual triage sweep of the entire registry's dynamic-analysis runs -- illustrating how rare confirmed intentional malware is in this ecosystem relative to npm/PyPI. Attack category: network C2 via third-party messaging API.
retrieved_context.source: manual triage, referenced in OSSF dynamic-analysis coverage discussion

retrieved_context.title: General pattern: proc-macro compiler-level injection
retrieved_context.text: Procedural macros execute inside the Rust compiler at compile time and can inject arbitrary code into the compiled binary, or exfiltrate the source code being compiled (a trade-secret theft vector distinct from runtime data theft). A legitimate proc-macro's implementation should not need std::net, std::process, or an HTTP client crate -- these are the strongest structural red flags for this attack surface, since a macro's job is token-stream transformation, not network I/O.

retrieved_context.title: CrateDepression / rustdecimal (2022)
retrieved_context.text: A coordinated typosquatting campaign where the crate 'rustdecimal' impersonated the legitimate 'rust_decimal' crate (52M+ downloads at the time). Edit distance from the target name was 1 (removed underscore). The malicious crate's build.rs deployed a Mythic C2 (command and control) agent specifically into GitLab CI/CD pipelines. The payload fingerprinted the environment before activating -- it only deployed inside detected CI systems, evading casual local testing. Attack category: typosquatting + backdoor + CI-targeting build.rs payload.
